title: 17 FREE Mac Apps You'll Actually Use
author: Stephen Robles
summary: A rundown of free or nearly-free macOS utilities chosen for removing daily friction rather than adding features: install and uninstall cleanup, clipboard and AirDrop shortcuts, menu-bar decluttering, and disk visibility. The implicit bar for inclusion is that an app lives in the menu bar, does its job in one click, and ideally exposes Shortcuts or Control Center actions. Several picks are framed as free alternatives that match paid tools. It closes on a built-in macOS setting most people never find — Archive Utility can delete the zip after expanding it.
takeaways: EasyDMG turns DMG installs into one step: right-click a .dmg, Get Info, Open With, choose EasyDMG, then Change All so it handles every future DMG — it installs, ejects and trashes the image.
Docky is pay-what-you-want: set animation delay to none and speed to instant for an immediately revealing hidden Dock. Robles entered $5 rather than $0.
Dock Door adds live window previews to Command-Tab and Dock icons, so multiple Safari profile windows become individually selectable rather than one blind target.
Two menu-bar managers compared: Thaw (GitHub, more features, profiles and hotkeys) versus Hidden Bar (Mac App Store, simpler, needs screen-recording permission granted manually).
App Cleaner removes an app's leftover files by drag-and-drop; the paid comparison is Hazel, whose Settings → Trash → App Sweep does it automatically on every delete.
Gnome is 'free-ish': after five minutes of use per session, GIF search returns only Weird Al results unless you pay $7 once. Stash is free to 10 saved items, $3 once for unlimited.
OmniDiskSweeper (from the OmniFocus and OmniGraffle makers) ranks storage highest to lowest across internal, external and network drives, with a caution to know what you are deleting.
The closing bonus is a years-old built-in setting: open Archive Utility via Spotlight or Raycast, and set 'after expanding, move archive to trash' so unzipping stops leaving the zip behind.
quotes: Now, I say it's free-ish because after 5 minutes of free usage, you can still use the app, but then it will only show you GIF search results for Weird Al.
If all you send are Weird Al GIFs, this is the perfect app for you.
You can put $0 and download it completely for free. I gave them five bucks because that feature, that was a worth it upgrade.
Again, be careful, make sure you know what you're deleting, but it's just a great way to see what's taking up the most storage, highest to lowest, right here.
You were all right telling me about Raycast for years.
All these options were here sitting in the Mac the whole time.
bestIdeas: Make the default handler do the work. Reassigning what opens a file type (DMG to EasyDMG) removes a repeated manual sequence permanently — a pattern worth applying to any file type you handle the same way every time.
Prefer a menu-bar utility with a Shortcuts action over a full app. His selection bar is a useful filter generally: does it live where I already am, and can it be scripted?
Check whether the OS already does it. The Archive Utility tip is a reminder that a long-standing built-in setting often beats installing something.
Uninstall is a first-class problem. Apps outside the App Store scatter files; deciding upfront how you will remove something is part of adopting it.
tools: EasyDMG — auto-installs from a DMG, then ejects and trashes the image.
Stash — cross-device clipboard and snippet store for text, links and GIFs; free to 10 items, $3 once for unlimited.
Menu Drop — AirDrops the clipboard, or any file dragged onto its menu-bar icon.
Share Shot — frames screenshots with auto device detection and gradient backgrounds; v2.0 adds free batch mode and redactions.
Docky — controls Dock auto-hide animation delay and speed; pay what you want.
Dock Door — window previews for Command-Tab and Dock icons, plus folder pop and alt-tab switching.
Kantan Timer Pro — drag-to-set menu-bar timers shown as on-screen countdown rings.
Thaw — menu-bar manager with hidden and always-hidden sections, hotkeys and profiles (GitHub).
Hidden Bar — simpler Mac App Store menu-bar manager with a global shortcut.
App Cleaner — drag an app in to find and remove its leftover files.
Keyboard Clean Tool — from the BetterTouchTool makers; disables keyboard input for cleaning, unlock by holding the trackpad 3 seconds.
Gnome — menu-bar GIF search with a global shortcut; free-ish, $7 once for unrestricted search.
OmniDiskSweeper — disk-space scanner ranking usage highest to lowest.
Clocker — multi-timezone menu-bar app with calendar events and a time scrubber for scheduling.
Disk View — menu-bar view of internal, external and network drive usage, with pin and eject.
Raycast — the launcher he has switched to, praised for aliases, quick keys and extensions on the free tier.
Archive Utility — the built-in macOS tool holding the trash-the-zip-after-expanding setting.
Also named in passing: HandBrake (free video conversion) and Hazel (paid file automation, used for App Sweep).
method: EasyDMG as default handler: right-click a .dmg → Get Info → Open With → EasyDMG → Change All.
Docky instant Dock: open preferences → animation delay 'none', speed 'instant' → save.
Gnome GIF search: assign a global shortcut (his is Shift-Option-Command-G), arrow to a result, Return copies it to the clipboard.
Hazel app sweep: Settings → Trash → enable App Sweep, so deleting an app offers its leftover files for trashing.

Archive Utility: search it in Spotlight or Raycast (nothing appears to open), then in its settings set 'after expanding, move archive to trash', optionally set a destination folder and reveal-in-Finder behaviour.

keyMessage: There is a whole tier of free Mac utilities that quietly remove everyday friction, and it is worth hunting them down rather than living with the defaults — sometimes the fix is already built into macOS.
